Subject: PHI dry-run for bulk patient notes ingestion — BAA applicability?

Hi Logan,

Thanks for chatting on the call earlier. We have a follow-up question from our engineering and privacy teams: InnoHealth is planning a short dry-run (internal testing only) to validate our bulk ingestion pipeline into Redwood for 2M patient notes (anonymized for now, but may include direct identifiers in later tests). Before we proceed we need confirmation on two points:

1) Would that dry-run be considered PHI processing under the BAA (i.e., do we need a signed BAA before any test data is accepted)?
2) If we keep the payload pseudonymized (patient_id replaced with a hash) and request zero retention/logging of payloads, is the hosted API acceptable or do we need Dedicated/Private?

I've attached a small sample payload and our proposed ingest architecture for context. Our Privacy Officer would like a short written note on whether Redwood considers the dry-run in-scope for a BAA and recommended deployment mode.

Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Emma

Subject: Re: PHI dry-run for bulk patient notes ingestion — BAA applicability?

Hi Emma — thanks for the detailed note and the attachments. Quick summary up front: we generally treat any data that can be tied to an identifiable patient as PHI for the purposes of a BAA. A dry-run with real identifiers or reversible pseudonyms would be in-scope. That said, there are technical mitigations that can make a hosted dry-run feasible for testing-only workloads.

Options we recommend (short-form):
- Dedicated test pool (recommended): provision a short-lived Dedicated environment (reserved capacity) for the dry-run. This gives isolation, configurable retention, and an auditable boundary — lowest friction for legal/privacy teams.
- Hosted with strong pseudonymization: if you irrevocably remove direct identifiers (replace patient_id with salted, non-reversible hashes), and sign an agreement that no production identifiers will be used, we can accept a one-off dry-run on hosted under an explicit temporary data-handling addendum. Note this requires our security team to review your pseudonymization method.
- Private/VPC (if regulations require): full private deployment is also an option but requires longer lead time.

Controls we will require for any path:
- No persistent token retention for the dry-run; we can disable request/response logging for the test tenant and configure zero retention for payloads.
- KV cache disabled for the ingestion endpoints and no long-term embedding storage.
- Short TTLs and automatic purge (we can set a 24–72 hour retention window for the dry-run).
- Encryption in transit and at rest (standard).
- Access to audit logs and redacted request traces for your review (we redact sensitive fields by default but can provide field-level guidance).

Next steps I suggest:
1) If you want isolation and the quickest path for legal sign-off, we provision a Dedicated test pool for 72 hours and run your dry-run there.
2) If you prefer hosted, please share a short description of the pseudonymization method and an example of a pre-processed record; we will route that to security for an expedited review.
3) We can prepare a short statement confirming that the dry-run will be considered out-of-scope for BAA if all controls are met and verified — but that statement must be explicit and conditional on the controls.

I've looped Karthik for the technical steps and to confirm how we would configure a Dedicated short-term test.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
attachments: ingest-dryrun-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 9KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PHI dry-run for bulk patient notes ingestion — BAA applicability?

Hi Emma — quick technical note from the SE side on what we can do for the dry-run and recommended defaults:

1) Ingestion mode: stream vs bulk
- For 2M notes we recommend our bulk ingest pipeline which supports chunked uploads and backpressure. For testing, a short-lived Dedicated pool (GPU or CPU depending on model) prevents noisy-neighbor issues.

2) Retention & logs
- We can set the tenant to no token logging and zero request/response persistence for the test window. Our default audit logs (who/when) remain but we can redact payload fields.

3) KV cache & embeddings
- KV cache will be disabled for the test endpoints to ensure no cached prefixes remain. We will also disable any embeddings being written to persistent stores.

4) Pseudonymization guidance
- Non-reversible salted hashes (HMAC with a customer-provided key) for patient_id is acceptable. Please avoid reversible encryption where Redwood or any middleware can decrypt.

5) Performance & errors
- We'll provide a short-run smoke test first (10k records) to validate parsing and rate limits, then scale up. We can throttle to your ingest pipeline to avoid spikes.

6) Evidence & BAA language
- We can provide a short written confirmation for your Privacy Officer that the dry-run would be out of BAA scope if the controls above are implemented and verified. If the payload contains direct identifiers or reversible IDs, a signed BAA is required beforehand.

If you want, we can spin up a Dedicated trial pool and a temporary test tenant tomorrow. I'll prepare the ops checklist and coordinate with infra.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
